why_regime_matters: Main annual stress regime and dominant source of 2023 upper-tail prices.
internal_evidence: Rows 4314; 111 of 120 annual £250+ periods; 18 of 21 annual £300+ periods; £250+ probability 2.57%; £300+ probability 0.42%.
main_price_mechanism: Broad regime-level stress combined with imbalance escalation, high gas, lower wind episodes, and strong evening-peak amplification.
external_context_needed: Winter margin conditions; interconnector flow/availability context; gas-market background; specific high-price days in Jan-Mar 2023.
paper_section_use: Core evidence for 2023 stress architecture and spike-realization section.
research_note: Treat Q1 2023 as the main structural stress regime, not simply a cluster of isolated spike events.

why_regime_matters: Main quiet baseline regime; useful contrast against Q1 stress.
internal_evidence: Rows 8783; only 1 £250+ period and 1 £300+ period; £250+ probability 0.01%; £100+ probability 39.16%.
main_price_mechanism: Mostly low-risk regime despite frequent low-wind periods; high-price stress rarely converted into spikes.
external_context_needed: Summer demand context; renewable/gas background; any isolated event explaining the single £250+/£300+ exception.
paper_section_use: Baseline comparison for proving low wind alone does not explain spike formation.
research_note: Important because Apr-Sep had low-wind exposure but almost no spikes, weakening any simple wind-only explanation.

why_regime_matters: Late-year transition regime where stress began to reappear but remained far below Q1 intensity.
main_price_mechanism: Localized high imbalance and high gas conditions with lower wind during upper-tail periods.
external_context_needed: Autumn system margin context; wind conditions; gas generation reliance; interconnector availability/flows.
paper_section_use: Transition-regime evidence showing stress can return without becoming the dominant annual regime.
research_note: Useful for comparing with 2024 Oct-Nov, which became much more important in that year.

why_regime_matters: Overall windy/low-price December regime, but with isolated extreme local stress events.
internal_evidence: Rows 1487; 2 £250+ periods; 1 £300+ period; Dec £250+ avg wind 866.5 MW and avg gas 26230 MW.
main_price_mechanism: Generally high-wind background, but rare local episodes of very low wind and extreme gas dependence produced spikes.
external_context_needed: Specific December low-wind days; gas generation context; interconnector flows; possible outage or system-margin events.
paper_section_use: Example of difference between regime background and local event condition.
research_note: Do not let the dec_windy label hide the fact that isolated spike periods were physically severe.

why_regime_matters: Direct contrast to 2023 Q1; shows early-year stress did not repeat in 2024.
main_price_mechanism: Quiet early-year regime with no upper-tail price realization despite normal winter system operation.
external_context_needed: Winter 2023/24 margin context; gas/wind background; interconnector conditions supporting lower stress.
paper_section_use: Cross-year comparison showing stress timing shifted away from Q1 in 2024.
research_note: This is a major reason the paper should compare regimes, not just years.

why_regime_matters: Large quiet baseline regime in 2024, reinforcing that Jan-Sep had almost no upper-tail stress.
internal_evidence: Rows 8784; 0 £250+ and 0 £300+ periods; only 1 £200+ period; £100+ probability 22.02%.
main_price_mechanism: Mostly normal-to-low price formation with very limited severe stress conversion.
external_context_needed: Summer demand and renewable output context; any explanation for the single £200+ exception.
paper_section_use: Baseline regime for 2024 and contrast against Oct-Nov/Dec late-year stress.
research_note: Shows 2024 was not continuously stressed; upper-tail risk was highly concentrated later in the year.

why_regime_matters: Important late-year transition regime that produced a large share of 2024 extreme prices.
internal_evidence: Rows 2928; 10 of 24 annual £250+ periods; 6 of 17 annual £300+ periods; £300+ avg imbalance 753.55 MW.
main_price_mechanism: Imbalance-escalation intense regime with low wind, high gas, and reduced interconnector support during extreme periods.
external_context_needed: Specific Oct-Nov low-wind events; imbalance/system stress days; interconnector availability/flow context; gas generation conditions.
paper_section_use: Key evidence that 2024 stress began before December and that Oct-Nov was not just a mild transition.
research_note: Do not describe 2024 only as December stress; Oct-Nov produced 10 of the 24 annual £250+ periods.

why_regime_matters: Main 2024 physical scarcity regime and strongest late-year stress block.
internal_evidence: Rows 1488; 14 of 24 annual £250+ periods; 11 of 17 annual £300+ periods; Dec £250+ avg wind 1471 MW and avg gas 27054.5 MW.
main_price_mechanism: Very low wind and extreme gas dependence, with high prices occurring across active daytime/evening periods rather than only evening peak.
external_context_needed: December 2024 dunkelflaute events; gas-fired generation reliance; winter margin context; interconnector flow/availability conditions.
paper_section_use: Core evidence for 2024 thermally extreme spike architecture.
research_note: 2024 had fewer spikes than 2023, but December spike conditions were more physically extreme.
